text: How many ciprofloxacin studies are there for Escherichai coli?
I'll search GEO for ciprofloxacin expression studies in Escherichia coli.

## Abstract

This report quantifies the number of ciprofloxacin-related gene expression studies deposited for *Escherichia coli* in the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). A single Series-level query was routed to GEO restricting the organism to *Escherichia coli* and requiring the free-text term "ciprofloxacin," returning a total of 37 GEO Series (GSE). Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic that targets bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, and it is a common model agent in studies of antibiotic tolerance, resistance evolution, and the bacterial stress response. The count of 37 was reported directly by GEO as the total number of matching Series; ten records were retrieved in detail for inspection. NCBI silently rewrote the submitted query through its MeSH mapping, expanding "ciprofloxacin" to include MeSH and all-fields synonyms, so the count reflects the rewritten query rather than the literal term. Inspected records spanned RNA-seq of antibiotic tolerance mutants, resistance-emergence adaptive evolution, nucleoid 3D-organization experiments that used ciprofloxacin as one perturbation, and comparative bactericidal-mechanism studies. Six of the ten inspected Series carried a linked PubMed identifier. The result establishes the current volume of reusable *E. coli* ciprofloxacin transcriptomic data and provides accessions for downstream retrieval.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** *Escherichia coli* is a Gram-negative bacterium and the principal model organism for bacterial genetics and physiology. Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic that inhibits DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV. Transcriptomic studies of *E. coli* under ciprofloxacin exposure are used to dissect antibiotic tolerance, resistance evolution, and stress-response regulation. The question of how many such studies exist establishes the volume of reusable data.

**Literature Review.** The GEO query returned Series with linked PubMed identifiers. Among the ten inspected records, the following PubMed links were reported by the tool: PMID 40879398 (GSE276254), PMID 40804527 (GSE283264, GSE272161, GSE272160, GSE272159, GSE272158), PMID 41805196 (GSE295494), PMID 42079445 (GSE292923), and PMID 39235234 (GSE275261). GSE309890 had no linked PubMed record. The abstract text of these papers was not fetched, only the GEO-registered links.

**Knowledge Gap.** Before this query, the number of ciprofloxacin-associated *E. coli* expression Series in GEO was not established here.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: to count the GEO Series matching *E. coli* and ciprofloxacin. No statistical hypothesis applies; this is an enumeration.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** GEO holds processed gene expression Series and is the appropriate resource for "expression studies" by organism and topic. The query was restricted to Series (GSE) entry type, the standard unit of study-level reuse.

**Materials.** NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (`gds` database), reached with the `geo_search` tool.

**Procedures.** One tool call was made:
- `geo_search` with `organism="Escherichia coli"`, `term="ciprofloxacin"`, `entry_type="gse"`, `max_results=10`.

The executed query, as reported by the tool, was `"Escherichia coli"[Organism] AND (ciprofloxacin) AND "gse"[Filter]`, which NCBI rewrote to `"Escherichia coli"[Organism] AND ("ciprofloxacin"[All Fields] OR "ciprofloxacin"[MeSH Terms] OR ciprofloxacin[All Fields]) AND "gse"[Filter]`.

**Statistical Analysis.** The headline number is the `total_count` field returned by GEO (37). This is the count of matching Series for the rewritten query; no deduplication was performed by this report. The organism filter explodes down the taxonomy, so it includes *E. coli* strains and mixed-organism Series. Ten Series were returned in full for inspection; the PubMed-link proportion (6 of 10, counting the two-organism GSE275261 and the SuperSeries/SubSeries of PMID 40804527) was tallied from the `pubmed_ids` field of the returned records only, not from all 37.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Count summary**

| Metric | Value | Source field |
|---|---|---|
| Total *E. coli* ciprofloxacin GEO Series | 37 | `total_count` |
| Records returned in detail | 10 | `returned` |
| Entry type | Series (GSE) | `entry_type` |

**Table 2. Inspected Series (first 10 of 37)**

| Accession | Taxon | Samples | Linked PMID | Public date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSE309890 | *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 | 6 | none | 2026/02/01 |
| GSE276254 | *E. coli* | 51 | 40879398 | 2025/08/25 |
| GSE283264 | *E. coli* | 25 | 40804527 | 2025/06/24 |
| GSE272161 | *E. coli* | 64 | 40804527 | 2025/06/24 |
| GSE272160 | *E. coli* | 4 | 40804527 | 2025/06/24 |
| GSE272159 | *E. coli* | 33 | 40804527 | 2025/06/24 |
| GSE272158 | *E. coli* | 2 | 40804527 | 2025/06/24 |
| GSE295494 | *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 | 42 | 41805196 | 2025/05/01 |
| GSE292923 | *E. coli* | 4 | 42079445 | 2025/03/25 |
| GSE275261 | *A. baumannii*; *E. coli* | 24 | 39235234 | 2024/08/25 |

**Findings.** GEO holds 37 Series matching *E. coli* and ciprofloxacin. Of the 10 Series inspected, 4 belong to one nucleoid-organization study (PMID 40804527, GSE272158–GSE272161 plus GSE283264), in which ciprofloxacin ("cipro") appears as one of several perturbation conditions rather than as the study focus. Two Series (GSE292923, GSE295494) are directly centered on ciprofloxacin transcriptional response. One Series (GSE275261) is a two-organism study also including *Acinetobacter baumannii*. One inspected Series (GSE309890) had no registered PubMed link.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** The objective is met: 37 GEO Series match the query. This is the count of Series where "ciprofloxacin" appears anywhere in the indexed record for an *E. coli* study, not necessarily 37 studies whose primary intervention was ciprofloxacin.

**Context.** Inspection of the first 10 records shows the count is heterogeneous: it mixes dedicated ciprofloxacin-response experiments (GSE292923, GSE295494) with studies where ciprofloxacin is one of many conditions (the PMID 40804527 group). Several Series from a single publication are counted individually, so the number of distinct studies is lower than the number of Series.

**Limitations.** NCBI rewrote the query through MeSH, so the count reflects the expanded term set, not the literal string "ciprofloxacin." The organism filter includes all descendant strains and mixed-organism Series (e.g., GSE275261 also covers *A. baumannii*). SuperSeries and their SubSeries are counted separately, inflating the Series count relative to the number of independent studies. Only 10 of 37 records were retrieved, so per-record fields (sample counts, PubMed links) describe only the inspected subset. GEO returns metadata only; no expression values were examined.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** There are 37 ciprofloxacin-associated *E. coli* GEO Series. To convert this into a count of distinct studies, the next query worth running is a de-duplication by linked BioProject or PubMed ID across all 37 records, or a restriction of the free-text term to the sample/treatment fields to exclude Series where ciprofloxacin is only incidental.

## References

[1] NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus, esearch (`gds` database). Query: `"Escherichia coli"[Organism] AND (ciprofloxacin) AND "gse"[Filter]`. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi
[2] GEO Series GSE309890. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[3] GEO Series GSE276254. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE276nnn/GSE276254/
[4] GEO Series GSE283264. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE283nnn/GSE283264/
[5] GEO Series GSE272161. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272161/
[6] GEO Series GSE272160. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272160/
[7] GEO Series GSE272159. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272159/
[8] GEO Series GSE272158. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272158/
[9] GEO Series GSE295494. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE295nnn/GSE295494/
[10] GEO Series GSE292923. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE292nnn/GSE292923/
[11] GEO Series GSE275261. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE275nnn/GSE275261/

## Acknowledgments

Data provided by the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and the submitting laboratories of the cited Series, accessed via NCBI E-utilities.

---

**Short answer: 37 GEO Series.** Note this is a Series count, not a count of independent studies — several of the 37 come from single publications (multiple SubSeries), and the MeSH-expanded query plus taxonomy-exploding organism filter inflate the number.
